title: The Only Cat Ever Sent to Space

scenes.voiceover: Every country sent dogs or monkeys to space. Only one country sent a cat. And almost no one remembers her.
scenes.mainText: ONLY ONE CAT HAS EVER GONE TO SPACE

scenes.voiceover: October 1963. France chose a former Paris street cat from fourteen candidates, and implanted electrodes in her skull to read her brain. Her name was Félicette.
scenes.mainText: A PARIS STRAY WITH ELECTRODES IN HER SKULL

scenes.voiceover: A rocket carried her past a hundred and fifty kilometers and back. Thirteen minutes later she was on the ground, alive. The only cat in space, and she survived it.
And then the story turns cold. Two months later, she was put down so scientists could study her brain. The autopsy, by most accounts, revealed almost nothing.
scenes.mainText: THEN THEY EUTHANIZED HER TO STUDY HER BRAIN

scenes.voiceover: For decades she was forgotten, and often misremembered as a male cat named Félix. Only recently did she get a statue. A small bronze cat, looking up.
scenes.mainText: FORGOTTEN FOR 50 YEARS. NOW, A STATUE.
scenes.visualConcept: Earth from space, a look upward.

scenes.voiceover: Félicette was one of many. Every animal we sent to space is on the channel.
scenes.mainText: EVERY ANIMAL WE SENT UP → ON THE CHANNEL
